Hi Sara — really appreciate the clear list. Quick answers up front, details below and attaching our proposed terms doc.

1) Minimum committed spend: We can offer a 6-month commit with monthly billing. Unused committed tokens are treated as credits that can be reallocated across models within the same billing account. They do not automatically roll over beyond the 6-month term unless you choose a renewal with a carry-forward option (we can add language if your procurement needs it).

2) Overage / burst: Standard behavior is: on-demand price applies to usage beyond the commit. For customers with predictable burst patterns we offer a burst multiplier: 1) up to 10% over commit = on-demand rate, 2) 10–50% over = on-demand + 15% discount off public on-demand (i.e., partially discounted), 3) >50% over = on-demand + 5% discount but subject to capacity windows. We can also enable a temporary burst pool (pre-purchased burst credits) at a discounted per-token rate for end-of-quarter spikes.

3) Credits across model types: Committed token credits are fungible across text-generation and embeddings in the same billing account, but we require a mapping table at signup for any specialized model variants (e.g., private finetune).

See attached "Redwood_Terms_Proposal_v3.pdf" — I've highlighted the minimum-spend clause and the overage appendix. I copied Rishi (finance) and Neha (legal) to confirm the language.

Next step: if procurement prefers a fixed floor with explicit burst credits, we can price a 25k token burst pack that sits aside and is consumed before applying overage. Let me know which construct you prefer and I can prepare a short exhibit.

Best,

Hi Jake / team — quick note from finance/ops on how we handle burst packs vs on-demand:

- If you purchase a burst pack, those tokens are consumed first. Once exhausted, requests default to the agreed overage (on-demand) rate; we do not silently throttle unless the customer is under an explicit capacity SLA that specifies throttling behavior.
- For customers who require guaranteed plateau throughput during spikes, we recommend Redwood Dedicated or a reserved burst buffer (a temporary dedicated pool) — that can be contracted as an add-on and will have a separate pricing line item.
- Example math (for clarity): your monthly commit = 10M tokens at $0.0009/token. On-demand = $0.0016/token. Burst pack = 250k tokens at $0.00095/token (prepaid). If you spend commit + burst pack and then use 20% more, the 20% overage would be billed at on-demand $0.0016 (unless you are in one of the banded discount tiers mentioned by Aditya).

I've updated the "overage" appendix in the attached redline with a numeric example and a short exhibit we can include. Happy to run your expected token histogram through our pricing simulator if you want a tailored quote.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Revenue Ops, Redwood Inference

Sara / Procurement team — a couple of legal points on the proposed draft:

- Minimum spend clause: we can include a carry-forward option limited to a single renewal period (i.e., unused credits can be applied to the first month of renewal only). If you need multi-term carry-forward we will need to evaluate commercially.
- Overage bands: recommend we explicitly enumerate the band thresholds and define how discounts are applied (we've added a simple table in the attached redline).
- Burst credits / prepaid packs: We'll add language clarifying that burst packs are prepaid, consumed FIFO after committed tokens, and will not be refundable.
- Audit & usage reporting: we will include a monthly usage report and a dedicated billing contact for any disputed charges; disputes must be raised within 60 days of invoice.

If this aligns with your procurement policy, we can produce a final document for signature.
